title: The Fruitlessness of Nominal Repentance
english: It was being demonstrated. So that having gathered [the points] I might say, the woman exerted repentance through all her senses and through her habits which had sinned; and it is possible to demonstrate by inference that she was mourning her sins publicly and in an obvious way, whereas she used to practice [sin] privately in her leisure. As for us, our promise announces repentance, but our practice shows nothing additional, but rather we maintain the same state of life which we lived even before the sin.

For brightness is the same, and the same clothing, and a luxurious enjoyment of the table, and long sleep relaxed into indolence, and various distractions and cares producing forgetfulness to the soul through its own self-care. But we are only inscribed with the name of repentance, being both unfruitful and inactive; separating ourselves from the mysteries and from the communion of the secret sanctifications, and making no effort at all for a return toward them, but rather despising the enjoyment as if it were easy.

Understand, man, that you are worthy of many things, yet you have been separated from the participation of those. If you were a participant at a royal table, and then, having struck against the honor, you were cast off, how much wealth would you spend to become a friend and table-fellow again? And what doors would you not have pursued, begging, being at a loss, groaning, considering life unlivable, manifesting the pain of the grief in the depths through rank and relation of person, moving every stone, even the stone of the word, until you had overcome the calamity for yourself?

But he who, having been separated from the intimacy toward God and having fallen from truly high honor, what great and significant thing of a corrupted soul will he demonstrate of humility? It is not consistent to say that one who is sick is changing to the same life as those who are healthy. For a different diet is for the sick one, and a different life for the healthy one.

See how great is the change of the well-off toward the condition of the ailing; for he, sensing the illness according to its state, lies down in a small room, having withdrawn from all habit, neglecting agriculture, being a very farmer, and abandoning concern for wealth...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Physician of the Soul
english: A speculator and a lover of money. He is nourished by water and pulse, even if formerly he was full of luxury and set a Sybaritic table. Separated from his usual marriage-bed, he does not delight children; he understands doctors both by night and by day, and for the sake of beloved profit, he hastens toward health with many wages. Such is the sick man of the body.

But he who is badly disposed regarding the soul, having surrounded the incorporeal [soul] with [physical] ailments, and feigning confession and showing weakness, leaves [it] to be devoured and torn apart by the passion, so that it might be spread out over the whole mass? But be temperate, know yourself: you have grieved God, having insulted your Creator, who has authority over this present life and is Lord and Judge of the life to come. Have you been harmed by luxury? Through fasting, heal the enjoyment. Has intemperance harmed the soul? Let temperance become the medicine for the sickness.

Has greed worked a many-layered fever upon the intellect? Let almsgiving empty the fullness, for it is the distribution of cleansing for those who have been filled. Has the seizing of others' things harmed us? Let the stolen thing return to its own master. Falsehood has brought us near to destruction; for he says, 'You shall perish, those who speak falsehood' (John 8:44); let studied truth stand against the danger.

A broken oath leads to the flying sickle of Zechariah threatening to cut the womb (Zech 9:1); let us put on the whole armor of repentance, so that we might repel the edge of the sickle. Has someone served impiously through heretical dogmas? Let him drive away superstition with the mindset of right belief. This indeed is repentance: a release and an undoing of those [things] formerly or according to practice being enacted, or according to disposition being thought.

But he who knows the usefulness of the seventy [times] of repentance, yet is always turning toward the filth of lawlessness, becomes a slave alongside one who knows the wrath of the master, yet in his presence works evil and triples the sin. Let him become sensitive toward the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Physician of the Soul
english: [It is] containing a disease. Crush yourself as much as you can; seek also the mourning of like-souled brothers to help you toward freedom. Show me your bitter and abundant tear, so that I may mix mine as well; take also the priest, a fellow-mourner of the affliction, as a father.

For who is such a false father or one adamant regarding the soul, as not to journey with the grieving children or to rejoice with them again? A priest is a son of [God] according to religion; he mourns sin just as Jacob [mourned] for Joseph's blood-stained tunic (Gen 37:31), as David [mourned] for Absalom's destruction, as Eli [mourned] for Hophni and Phinehas falling in the battle line, as Moses [mourned] for the people who innovated the godless calf-making (Ex 32).

Be emboldened before the [One] who begot you according to God, before the bodily fathers; show Him unashamedly the hidden things, strip bare the soul's secrets as one showing a hidden disease to a physician; He himself will attend to both decency and the cure; for the shame of parents touches those whom they have suffered. For the glory of those who begot is likewise their shame. The term of life is uncertain, brothers. Let us outpace the departure through care.

For it is absurd that those who calculate their providence according to the flesh cleanse themselves from material things before the circumcision of the so-called dog, lest the moisture that causes disease should work rot through excessive heat; but those who need care according to the intellect do not outrun the uncertainty of death and the heat of the testing fire, which burns unbidden and is never quenched.

You had the evangelical drachma and were enriching yourself well with the money, then through laziness you lost it. Light the lamp of repentance (Matt 25:1), bow down with care, seek the treasure hidden to the poor through afflictions (Matt 13:44). Having found it, lift it up and save it, so that we neighbors may rejoice with you in the joy in Christ, to whom glory is due, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
